correctness.rationale: The first real zero equals the minimum of the block Bessel first zeros divided by each block operator norm: the Fourier transform factorizes and singular vectors attain each threshold. Multiplying the unit-ball volumes by |det A| turns Hadamard equality into orthogonality of all scaled columns, yielding the complete optimizer class. Each normalized block is a contraction; trace(T^T T)≤d and scalar λ-1-log λ≥(sqrt λ-1)^2 prove the Frobenius polar-distance bound. A two-block shear has logarithmic deficit and squared orthogonal distance both asymptotic to ε²/2, proving exponent sharpness. Stirling and published Bessel first-zero asymptotics yield the stated entropy law with the positive-proportion error rate. Standalone matrix/Bessel checker passed 409 configurations. No finite test substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The first real Fourier zero is a natural convex-body isoperimetric invariant, recently shown globally unbounded in dimensions at least three. The result supplies a complete sharp finite-dimensional optimization and equality classification for a curved, infinite-dimensional family of affine product geometries, a dimension-free stability theorem with optimal square-root exponent, and the factor-entropy high-dimensional loss. It differentiates product obstructions from the known bipyramidal global counterexamples. This is mathematically motivated geometric rigidity rather than an arbitrary parameter computation. The estimate coefficient is not asserted optimal, and no global body-class bound is claimed.
